findings_qualitative.value: HCN(1-0)/HCO+(1-0) and HCN(4-3)/CS(7-6) show overlap between AGN-dominated CND and starburst-dominated SB ring regions across spatial scales, making them insufficient as unique diagnostics.

evidence.quote: For the HCN(1-0)/HCO$^+$(1-0) and HCN(4-3)/CS(7-6) ratios, we observe an overlap in the observed ranges of these ratios between AGN-dominated and SB-dominated regions.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN(4-3)/HCO+(4-3) separates CND and SB regions at both high (~40 pc) and low (>=100 pc) resolutions, while HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) reliably separates them only at high spatial resolution (< 50 pc).

evidence.quote: We propose that at high spatial resolution (\< 50 pc) the HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) is a reliable tracer of AGN activity.

HCN(4-3)/HCO$^+$(4-3), on the other hand, seems to be distinctively higher in all the regions closer to the AGN position, at least at higher spatial resolutions. This distinction is even maintained when the ratio is viewed at lower-resolution scales, although the separation does decrease.

findings_qualitative.value: Variations in molecular line ratios between CND and SB regions are driven by differences in relative chemical abundances (HCN relative to HCO+ and CS) rather than differences in gas density or kinetic temperature.

evidence.quote: We also find that the variations in ratios are not a consequence of different densities or temperature but of different fractional abundances, yielding to the important result that it is essential to consider the chemical processes at play when drawing conclusions from radiative transfer calculations.

claims.hypothesis: Previously proposed molecular line ratios HCN(1-0)/HCO+(1-0) and HCN(4-3)/CS(7-6) reliably separate AGN-dominated regions from starburst-dominated regions.
claims.experiment: Compiled and re-analysed ALMA, PdBI, and JCMT observations of NGC 1068 across 10 sub-regions at ~40 pc and >=100 pc spatial scales, corrected for beam dilution, and compared ratio distributions between CND and SB ring regions.
claims.result: In the SB region NSB-c, HCN(1-0)/HCO+(1-0) is 3.09 +/- 0.44 (exceeding most CND regions), while HCN(4-3)/CS(7-6) ranges overlap significantly between CND (7.82 to 20.3) and SB regions (1.27 to 7.12 with large errors) even at ~40 pc resolution.
claims.finding: HCN(1-0)/HCO+(1-0) and HCN(4-3)/CS(7-6) do not reliably distinguish AGN from starburst activity regardless of spatial scale.

evidence.quote: For the HCN(1-0)/HCO$^+$(1-0) and HCN(4-3)/CS(7-6) ratios, we observe an overlap in the observed ranges of these ratios between AGN-dominated and SB-dominated regions.
We have found that previously proposed ratios such as HCN(1-0)/HCO+(1-0) and HCN(4-3)/CS(7-6) do not appear to be sufficient regardless of the spatial scale investigated

claims.hypothesis: The ratios HCN(4-3)/HCO+(4-3) and HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) can serve as reliable tracers of AGN-dominated gas at high spatial resolution.
claims.experiment: Measured HCN(4-3)/HCO+(4-3) and HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) across CND and SB sub-regions at high (~40 pc) and low (>=100 pc) spatial resolutions.
claims.result: At ~40 pc resolution, HCN(4-3)/HCO+(4-3) is >= 1.49 in CND regions vs <= 0.81 in SB regions, and HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) is >= 3.14 in CND regions vs <= 0.69 in SB regions (with NSB-c 3-sigma upper limit ~1.4); at >=100 pc, HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) in SSB-a rises to 5.39 +/- 0.97.
claims.finding: HCN(4-3)/HCO+(4-3) distinguishes AGN and SB regions at both high and low resolution, and HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) is a reliable tracer of AGN activity at high spatial resolution (< 50 pc).

evidence.quote: We propose that at high spatial resolution (\< 50 pc) the HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) is a reliable tracer of AGN activity.

HCN(4-3)/HCO$^+$(4-3), on the other hand, seems to be distinctively higher in all the regions closer to the AGN position, at least at higher spatial resolutions. This distinction is even maintained when the ratio is viewed at lower-resolution scales, although the separation does decrease.

claims.hypothesis: Differences in molecular line ratios between AGN-dominated CND regions and starburst-dominated SB ring regions are caused by differences in underlying chemical abundances rather than gas density or temperature.
claims.experiment: Performed LTE and non-LTE (RADEX via SpectralRadex) radiative transfer modelling coupled with MCMC sampling (12 walkers, 100,000 steps) to fit observed line ratios and derive posterior distributions of T_K, n_H2, and column density ratios.
claims.result: Posterior distributions of gas density and temperature are largely unconstrained and similar between CND and SB regions, whereas posterior column density ratios N(HCN)/N(HCO+) and N(HCN)/N(CS) are systematically higher in CND regions than in SB regions at ~40 pc resolution.
claims.finding: Variations in the molecular line ratios are driven by differences in fractional chemical abundances rather than gas density or temperature, making chemical modelling essential.

evidence.quote: What we observe at our highest resolution is that the best fitting `RADEX` models typically have higher abundances of HCN relative to both HCO$^+$ and CS within the AGN-dominated CND regions when compared to the best fitting models of the SB-dominated SB ring regions.

We investigated the origin of the differences in ratios and found that differences in gas densities and temperatures are not the cause of the differentiation. Upon computing the relative fractional abundances of HCN, HCO$^+$, and CS, we in fact determined that these differences are a consequence of differences in chemical abundances.

why_this_data.value: NGC 1068 is a nearby (~14 Mpc), bright archetypal composite AGN/SB galaxy with extensive multi-resolution archival observations of dense gas tracers HCN, HCO+, and CS from parsec to kiloparsec scales.

evidence.quote: NGC 1068 is a Seyfert 2 barred spiral galaxy; it is also the archetypal composite AGN/SB galaxy. Its close proximity ($\sim$14 Mpc) and significant brightness ($L_{Bol}$ $\approx$ 2.5 – 3.0 $10^{11}L_{\odot}$ ) (cite: Bland-Hawthorn_1997; Bock_2000) enable studies at many different resolutions, down to parsec scales

Despite the plethora of available published data focused on NGC 1068, within this study we focus on the dense gas tracers: HCN, HCO$^+$, and CS. This focus is in an effort to validate previously proposed ratios and diagrams rather than to suggest new ones.

why_this_method.value: Grouping data by spatial resolution with beam-dilution deconvolution prevents mixing disparate scales, while non-LTE RADEX modelling with MCMC sampling separates physical excitation effects (temperature, density) from chemical abundance variations.

evidence.quote: The different spatial resolutions make it necessary to ensure that only similarly obtained detections are compared. **This is especially true for the higher-resolution observations that cover only a small area of the galaxy.**

evidence.loc: Physical and chemical properties of NGC 1068
evidence.quote: To achieve this, we used radiative transfer modelling to infer the gas conditions and molecular column densities at each location for each resolution. We were then able to determine whether there are physical differences in excitation conditions between locations, differences in the underlying chemical abundances, or even a combination of the two

limitations_admitted.value: Not all sub-regions have been observed at all spatial resolutions for all molecules; NSB-b lacks consistent resolution observations and NSB-c has only a single high-resolution ratio (with HCN(4-3) and HCO+(4-3) below 3 sigma), excluding NSB-c from RADEX fitting.

evidence.quote: We note that not all sub-regions listed in Table [1](#tab:Regions), and shown in Figures [1](#fig:HCO$^+$) and [2](#fig:HCN), have been observed at all resolutions for all molecules.

The region NSB-c possesses fewer observed ratios than the other regions, with just a single high-resolution observation (see Table [2](#tab:Ratios)). As a result it is not included in the `RADEX` fitting discussed later in this paper.

limitations_admitted.value: Gas kinetic temperature, gas density (except in E Knot, W Knot, and NSB-a at 40 pc), and linewidth are poorly constrained by the MCMC RADEX fitting across resolutions.

evidence.quote: Neither the CND nor the SB ring regions can be reasonably constrained in the temperature or density planes, at least with regards to showing distinguishing qualities within these parameters.

limitations_admitted.value: Follow-up studies of other nearby galaxies are required to confirm whether HCN(4-3)/HCO+(4-3) and HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) hold as reliable diagnostics beyond NGC 1068.

evidence.quote: whereas HCN(4-3)/HCO+(4-3) HCN(4-3)/CS(2-1) may show promise at certain resolutions but follow up studies, especially of other nearby galaxies, is required in order to confirm our findings.

referee_caveats_inferred: Fitting 6 free parameters (n_H2, T_K, Delta v, N_HCN, N_HCO+, N_CS) to at most 4 observed line ratios per region leaves the system underconstrained, explaining the wide posterior uncertainties in temperature and density.

Assuming a single uniform sphere with identical T_K, n_H2, and linewidth for transitions with very different critical densities and upper-state energies (e.g., CS(2-1) vs HCN(4-3)) ignores multi-phase gas structure along the line of sight.

Deconvolving interferometric intensities using a simple Gaussian beam-dilution formula rather than uv-tapering or smoothing visibilities to a common beam can introduce systematic errors due to spatial filtering and clumpy emission morphology.
